Background & History

▼

Properties Analyzed:

  • P5063: Interlingual Index (ILI) - Single-value property linking a Wikidata entity to a concept in the Global WordNet Association's Collaborative Interlingual Index
  • P8814: WordNet 3.1 Synset ID - Unique-value property linking a Wikidata entity to a WordNet synset

Constraint Types:

PropertyConstraintMeaningViolation Type
P5063Single valueEach Wikidata item should have at most one ILIItem has multiple ILIs
P5063Unique valueEach ILI should map to only one Wikidata itemILI maps to multiple items
P8814Unique valueEach synset ID should map to only one Wikidata itemSynset maps to multiple items

Initial Problem (from Wikidata reports):

  • P5063: 17 single-value + 178 unique-value violations = 195 total
  • P8814: 2,146 violations (synsets with multiple QIDs)
  • Note: Our live SPARQL query found more violations as Wikidata has grown

Initial Approach (Discarded):

  • Parsed static markdown files from Wikidata constraint report page
  • Abandoned because: static data, parsing complexity, maintenance burden
  • Files deleted: P5063violations.md, P8814violations.md, missingILIs.csv

Current Approach:

  • Direct SPARQL queries via fetch_violations.py
  • Always current data from Wikidata
  • Cross-references with OEWN/OENN YAML to get synset definitions, members, and metadata
  • Joins with source data to provide full context for each violation

Key Insights:

  • Many "violations" are actually valid mappings representing different perspectives
  • Same entity can have multiple ILIs from OEWN and OENN (different names for same thing)
  • Same concept can have different parts of speech (noun vs verb)
  • Polysemy: single word with multiple meanings, all valid
  • True errors are duplicate ILIs added by mistake or stale mappings

Methodology

▼

Work done:

  1. Data Collection: Queried Wikidata SPARQL for live P5063 and P8814 constraint violations
  2. Enrichment: Joined with OEWN/OENN synset data (definitions, members, ILIs)
  3. Categorization:
    • P8814: Used label matching + description similarity to identify real vs. valid duplicates
    • P5063: Used synset definition matching to identify valid ILI mappings
    • Polysemy detection: Identified cases where multiple valid mappings exist for different senses
    • POS conflict detection: Identified valid cases where different parts of speech map to same concept
    • Similarity matching: Token-based comparison of synset definitions vs Wikidata descriptions
  4. 100% Coverage: All violations categorized (0% REVIEW remaining)

Next steps:

  1. Review the categorization in this dashboard
  2. Manually verify borderline cases (medium confidence)
  3. Generate QuickStatements for real violations
  4. Discuss with WordNet community
